faq.question: What is the difference between Retatrutide and Tirzepatide?
faq.answer: Retatrutide adds a third receptor target — the glucagon receptor (GCGR) — to the GIP/GLP-1 dual agonism of Tirzepatide. The glucagon component drives increased energy expenditure and lipolysis. Published data show ~24% body weight reduction with Retatrutide compared to ~21% with Tirzepatide at maximum research doses.

faq.question: Why is Retatrutide more difficult to manufacture?
faq.answer: Retatrutide's complexity arises from engineering balanced triple-receptor agonism into a single 39-amino-acid peptide. Achieving the correct potency ratio across GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors requires precise amino acid substitutions and the C20 fatty diacid linker. Each receptor's activation profile must be tuned so that none dominates or is suppressed.
